cards.explanation: The answer is to flee to the fortified cities. The horn is a run-for-cover signal, friends. The cry says, “Assemble yourselves and let us flee to the fortified cities.” Nobody is told to stop and think it over. When that horn blows, the walls are the plan.

The answer is False. The LORD speaks up about His part, friends. He says, “For I am bringing disaster from the north, and terrible destruction.” He doesn't hide behind the army or the lion. The text puts the disaster in His own words.

The answer is that he has set out to lay waste the land. The verse is blunt about it, friends: “He has left his lair to lay waste your land.” The cities will be reduced to ruins and lie uninhabited. A lion that leaves his lair isn't out for a stroll. I think this is the heaviest picture in the whole passage so far.

The answer is sackcloth. Verse 8 says, “So put on sackcloth, mourn and wail…” Sackcloth is what you wear when the heart is heavy, friends. Nobody is picking an outfit for style here. The reason given is that “…the fierce anger of the LORD has not turned away from us.”

The answer is peace. Jeremiah says the people were told, “You will have peace…” while a sword is at their throats. Look at the gap between the promise and the sword, friends. Peace was the word they heard, and the sword was the danger Jeremiah saw.

The answer is False. Verse 11 says the wind blows “…but not to winnow or to sift…” Verse 12 adds, “…a wind too strong for that comes from Me.” Then the LORD says, “Now I also pronounce judgments against them.” So this is no gentle sorting job, friends.

The answer is True. Verse 13 says, “His horses are swifter than eagles.” Eagles are about as fast as anything gets in the sky, friends. Picture those horses outrunning them. I can't catch a cookie rolling off the counter, so this speed is way beyond me.

The answer is the evil from her heart. Verse 14 says, “Wash the evil from your heart, O Jerusalem, so that you may be saved.” The call goes to the heart, friends, not just to the surface. It comes with a question too: “How long will you harbor wicked thoughts within you?” The alarm is loud, but this word is for the inside.

The answer is that she has rebelled against Him. The LORD says they surround her “…because she has rebelled against Me…” The reason comes from His own mouth, friends, so there's no guessing. The army surrounds her like men guarding a field. The text gives rebellion as the reason.

The answer is bitter and piercing to the heart. The LORD says, “This is your punishment; how bitter it is, because it pierces to the heart!” Right before that He says, “Your ways and deeds have brought this upon you.” I think this one is heavy, friends, so let's let it be heavy for a moment. The text makes it clear this isn't a small thing.

The answer is the horn and the alarm of battle. The voice says, “For I have heard the sound of the horn, the alarm of battle.” That's why the heart is pounding and the voice can't stay silent, friends. After that sound, anyone would be shaken. I think this person is hurting.
The answer is in an instant. The cry says, “My tents are destroyed in an instant, my curtains in a moment.” It doesn't happen slowly, friends. That's a lot to lose that fast. I think this one stings.

The answer is evil. The LORD says, “They are skilled in doing evil, but they know not how to do good.” It's a hard thing to hear, friends, and He says it about people He calls His own. Just before, He calls them “…foolish children, without understanding.” I think this is a sad line.

The answer is quaking and swaying. The one speaking says, “I looked at the mountains, and behold, they were quaking; all the hills were swaying.” Mountains are supposed to be the steady things, friends. When they shake, nothing feels safe. This is a scary picture.

The answer is False. Verse 25 says, “I looked, and no man was left; all the birds of the air had fled.” Not even the birds stayed, friends. It's a very quiet and empty scene. I think that quiet is part of what makes it heavy.

The answer is desert. Verse 26 says, “I looked, and the fruitful land was a desert.” What was once fruitful is now dry and bare, friends. The cities are “…torn down before the LORD, before His fierce anger.” It's a hard thing to see.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “The whole land will be desolate, but I will not finish its destruction.” The desolation is real, friends, and so is the limit He names. He doesn't say how or why here, so I won't guess. I'll just hold onto what He actually said.

The answer is no, He will not turn back. The LORD says, “I have spoken, I have planned, and I will not relent or turn back.” Those are firm words, friends. He says the earth will mourn and the heavens will grow dark. He is clear and He is not changing course.

The answer is True. Verse 29 says, “Every city is abandoned; no inhabitant is left.” First they flee into the thickets and climb among the rocks, friends. Then the cities sit empty. That's a very still picture.

The answer is that they despise her. Verse 30 says, “your lovers despise you; they want to take your life.” All the scarlet, the gold jewelry and the eye paint don't change that, friends. The text says she adorns herself in vain. Dressing up can't fix this.

The answer is murderers. The Daughter of Zion cries, “Woe is me, for my soul faints before the murderers!” She is gasping for breath and stretching out her hands, friends. I think this is one of the saddest cries in the passage. Let's let it be sad.
